L144: ### 2.3 Idempotents in $\mathbf{HK}_{\Theta}$
L145: 
L146: For $X\subseteq V_{\Theta}$, denote by $\Theta[X]$ the full subgraph of $\Theta$ with vertex set $X$, that is, $\Theta[X]$ is an oriented graph with vertex set $X$ and for $x_{i},x_{j}\in X$, there is an arrow from $x_{i}$ to $x_{j}$ in $\Theta[X]$ if and only if there is an arrow from $x_{i}$ to $x_{j}$ in $\Theta$.

L148: In (cite23†Forsberg, 2017 , Theorem 3.6), the following theorem is proved for a general finite simple oriented graph $\Theta$.
L149: ###### Theorem 2.5.
L150: 
L151: There is a bijection between idempotents in $\mathbf{HK}_{\Theta}$ and full subgraphs of $\Theta$ which do not contain any oriented cycles.
L152: 
L153: In the proof, an idempotent is mapped to the full subgraph of $\Theta$ whose vertex set is the content of the idempotent. Therefore, for each $X\subseteq V_{\Theta}$ such that $\Theta[X]$ does not contain any oriented cycles, there exists exactly one idempotent in $\mathbf{HK}_{\Theta}$ with content $X$. We denote this idempotent by $e_{X}$.

L430: ## 4 Homomorphisms from $\mathbf{HK}_{\Gamma}$ to $\mathbf{HK}_{\Theta}$
L431: 
L432: In this section, we study the set $\mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf{HK}_{\Gamma},\mathbf{HK}_{\Theta})$ of all monoid homomorphisms from $\mathbf{HK}_{\Gamma}$ to $\mathbf{HK}_{\Theta}$.
L433: ###### Theorem 4.1.
L434: 
L435: Let $\varphi:\{y_{1},y_{2},\dots,y_{m}\}\to\mathbf{HK}_{\Theta}$ be a map defined on the generators of $\mathbf{HK}_{\Gamma}$. The map $\varphi$ extends to a monoid homomorphism from $\mathbf{HK}_{\Gamma}$ to $\mathbf{HK}_{\Theta}$ if and only if there exist sets $X_{1},X_{2},\dots,X_{m}$ with $X_{i}\subseteq V_{\Theta}$ such that, for all $i,j\in\{1,2,\dots,m\}$, the following conditions hold:
L436: 
L437:   1. (i)
L438: 
L439: $X_{i}\in\mathcal{A}_{\Theta}$;
L440: 
L441:   2. (ii)
L442: 
L443: $\varphi(y_{i})=e_{X_{i}}$;
L444:   3. (iii)
L445: 
L446: $p_{\Theta}(X_{i},X_{j})$ and $p_{\Theta}(X_{j},X_{i})$ both hold if $y_{i}$ and $y_{j}$ are not connected in $\Gamma$;
L447: 
L448:   4. (iv)
L449: 
L450: $p_{\Theta}(X_{i},X_{j})$ holds if $y_{i}\overset{\Gamma}{\to}y_{j}$.
L451: ###### Proof.
L452: Assume that the map $\varphi$ extends to a monoid homomorphism from $\mathbf{HK}_{\Gamma}$ to $\mathbf{HK}_{\Theta}$, which we also denote by $\varphi$. Since a monoid homomorphism maps idempotents to idempotents, $\varphi(y_{i})$ is an idempotent in $\mathbf{HK}_{\Theta}$ for all $i\in\{1,2,\dots,m\}$. By Proposition cite38†2.7 , $\varphi(y_{i})$ is of the form $e_{X}$ for some $X\in\mathcal{A}_{\Theta}$.

L30: # Endomorphisms of Hecke–Kiselman Monoids Associated to Simple Oriented Graphs
L31: 
L32: Luka Andrenšek
L33: ###### Abstract
L34: Let $\mathrm{HK}_{\Theta}$ denote the Hecke–Kiselman monoid associated to a finite simple oriented graph $\Theta$. We reduce the problem of describing the endomorphism monoid $\mathrm{End}(\mathrm{HK}_{\Theta})$ to determining when a product of two idempotents in $\mathrm{HK}_{\Theta}$ is again an idempotent. This yields a procedure for constructing a Boolean matrix monoid isomorphic to $\mathrm{End}(\mathrm{HK}_{\Theta})$.
L35: As an application, we obtain an explicit description of the endomorphism monoid of the Catalan monoid $\mathcal{C}_{n+1}$.
L36: ###### keywords
L37: 
L38: Hecke–Kiselman monoid, endomorphism monoid, idempotent, Catalan monoid, Boolean matrix monoid
L39: ## 1 Introduction and Main Results
L40: 
L41: Let $\Theta=(V,E)$ be a finite simple oriented graph, that is, a finite oriented graph with no loops and at most one edge between any two vertices. If there is an arrow from $i$ to $j$, we write $i\to j$. If there are no arrows $i\to j$ or $j\to i$ and $i\neq j$, we say that $i$ and $j$ are not connected.
L42: In cite17†Ganyushkin and Mazorchuk (2011) , Ganyushkin and Mazorchuk define the Hecke–Kiselman monoid $\mathrm{HK}_{\Theta}$ associated to $\Theta$ as the monoid generated by idempotents
L43: 
L44:  | $$\{x_{i}\mid i\in V\}$$  |
L45: 
L46: subject to the following defining relations for all $i,j\in V$:
L47: 
L48:   * •
L49: 
L50: $x_{i}x_{j}=x_{j}x_{i}$ if $i$ and $j$ are not connected;
L51: 
L52:   * •
L53: 
L54: $x_{i}x_{j}x_{i}=x_{j}x_{i}x_{j}=x_{i}x_{j}$ if $i\to j$.
L55: 
L56: We denote by $e$ the unit element of $\mathrm{HK}_{\Theta}$.
L57: Hecke–Kiselman monoids were originally introduced in the setting of simple mixed graphs cite17†Ganyushkin and Mazorchuk (2011) . They have been studied by various authors cite18†Aragona and D’Andrea (2013) ; cite19†Aragona and D’Andrea (2020) ; cite20†Ashikhmin et al. (2015) ; cite21†Collina and D’Andrea (2015) ; cite22†Forsberg (2017) ; cite17†Ganyushkin and Mazorchuk (2011) ; cite23†Lebed (2025) ; cite24†Wiertel (2024) .
L58: Particular interest has been devoted to the corresponding Hecke–Kiselman algebras cite25†Okniński and Wiertel (2020) ; cite26†Okniński (2021) ; cite27†Wiertel (2022) ; cite28†Wiertel (2023) .
L59: From the proof of (cite17†Ganyushkin and Mazorchuk, 2011 , Theorem 16), it follows that every monoid isomorphism $\varphi:\mathrm{HK}_{\Theta}\to\mathrm{HK}_{\Theta^{\prime}}$ induces a graph isomorphism $f_{\varphi}:\Theta\to\Theta^{\prime}$ and every graph isomorphism $f:\Theta\to\Theta^{\prime}$ induces a monoid isomorphism $\varphi^{f}:\mathrm{HK}_{\Theta}\to\mathrm{HK}_{\Theta^{\prime}}$.
L60: Setting $\Theta^{\prime}=\Theta$, it can be verified that the automorphism group of $\mathrm{HK}_{\Theta}$ is isomorphic to the automorphism group of the graph $\Theta$. To the best of our knowledge, the structure and properties of endomorphisms of Hecke–Kiselman monoids have not been systematically explored.
L61: A description of endomorphisms of the Kiselman monoid cite29†D’Andrea and Stella (2023) ; cite30†Kiselman (2002) ; cite31†Kudryavtseva and Mazorchuk (2009) , which is the Hecke–Kiselman monoid corresponding to the full acyclic oriented graph, is known in the literature cite32†Andrenšek (2025) . In this paper, we adapt ideas from cite32†Andrenšek (2025) to study the endomorphism monoid of $\mathrm{HK}_{\Theta}$.
L62: For a positive integer $k$, we denote $[k]=\{1,2,\dots,k\}$. Throughout the paper, we assume $V=[n]$ for some positive integer $n$. In Section cite7†2 , we define $A_{\Theta}$ to be the set of all subsets $X\subseteq V$ such that the full subgraph of $\Theta$ with vertex set $X$ does not contain any oriented cycles. It is shown that for each $X\in A_{\Theta}$, there exists a unique idempotent $e_{X}$ in $\mathrm{HK}_{\Theta}$ with content $X$.
L63: 
L64: For $X,Y\in A_{\Theta}$, we define the predicate $p(X,Y)$ by
L65:  | $$p(X,Y):\!\iff e_{X}e_{Y}\text{ is an idempotent in }\mathrm{HK}_{\Theta}.$$  |
L66: 
L67: We define $(\Theta,p)$-pure sequences of subsets of $[n]$ to be sequences $(X_{1},X_{2},\dots,X_{n})$ such that, for all $i,j\in[n]$, the following conditions are satisfied:
L68: 
L69:   1. (i)
L70: 
L71: $X_{i}\in A_{\Theta}$;
L72: 
L73:   2. (ii)
L74: 
L75: $p(X_{i},X_{j})$ and $p(X_{j},X_{i})$ hold if $i$ and $j$ are not connected;
L76: 
L77:   3. (iii)
L78: 
L79: $p(X_{i},X_{j})$ holds if $i\to j$.
L80: We denote the set of all such sequences by $S_{n}(\Theta,p)$. We further define a natural binary operation $\ast$ on $S_{n}(\Theta,p)$ and show that it becomes a monoid with this operation.
L81: 
L82: The main result of this paper is that
L83: 
L84:  | $$\mathrm{End}(\mathrm{HK}_{\Theta})\cong S_{n}(\Theta,p).$$  |
L85: Using the characteristic-matrix encoding of such sequences, we then obtain a Boolean matrix monoid isomorphic to $\mathrm{End}(\mathrm{HK}_{\Theta})$. Finally, we use this framework to concretely describe all endomorphisms of the Catalan monoid $\mathcal{C}_{n+1}$.
L86: The paper proceeds as follows. In Section cite7†2 , we recall some results on Hecke–Kiselman monoids which we use throughout the paper. In Section cite11†3 , we present and prove the main result and illustrate it in the case when $\mathrm{HK}_{\Theta}$ is isomorphic to the Kiselman monoid. This example is included merely for illustration, since all endomorphisms of the Kiselman monoid are already known in the literature.
L87: The paper concludes with Section cite14†4 , where we derive an explicit description of all endomorphisms of the Catalan monoid, which is a novel result.
L88: ## 2 Preliminaries
L89: ### 2.1 The Content Map
L90: 
L91: For a word $w$ over the alphabet $\{x_{1},x_{2},\dots,x_{n}\}$, we define its content as the set of indices $i$ for which $x_{i}$ appears in $w$. Since the defining relations of $\mathrm{HK}_{\Theta}$ preserve content, we can define the content $c(x)$ for $x\in\mathrm{HK}_{\Theta}$ as the content of any word which represents $x$. Moreover, we have
L92: 
L93:  | $$c(xy)=c(x)\cup c(y)\quad\text{and}\quad c(e)=\emptyset,$$  |
L94: which shows that $c:\mathrm{HK}_{\Theta}\to\mathbbm{2}^{[n]}$ is a monoid epimorphism, where $\mathbbm{2}^{[n]}$ is equipped with the operation $\cup$.
L95: 
L96: We use the following lemma in the proof of Theorem cite33†3.4 .
L97: ###### Lemma 2.1.
L98: 
L99: Let $\psi,\varphi\in\mathrm{End}(\mathrm{HK}_{\Theta})$. Then
L100: 
L101:  | $$c((\psi\circ\varphi)(x_{i}))=\bigcup_{j\in c(\varphi(x_{i}))}c(\psi(x_{j})).$$  |
L102: ###### Proof.
L103: 
L104: If $\varphi(x_{i})=e$, then we have $c(\varphi(x_{i}))=\emptyset$ and $(\psi\circ\varphi)(x_{i})=e$. Hence $c((\psi\circ\varphi)(x_{i}))=\emptyset$, and thus the conclusion holds in this case.
L105: 
L106: Now suppose $\varphi(x_{i})\neq e$ and write $\varphi(x_{i})=x_{i_{1}}\dots x_{i_{k}}$ for some $k\geq 1$ and $i_{1},\dots,i_{k}\in V$. Then $c(\varphi(x_{i}))=\{i_{1},\dots,i_{k}\}$ and we further have
L107:  | $$(\psi\circ\varphi)(x_{i})=\psi(x_{i_{1}}\dots x_{i_{k}})=\psi(x_{i_{1}})\dots\psi(x_{i_{k}}).$$  |
L108: 
L109: Hence we have
L110: 
L111:  | $$c((\psi\circ\varphi)(x_{i}))=c(\psi(x_{i_{1}}))\cup\dots\cup c(\psi(x_{i_{k}})),$$  |
L112: 
L113: and therefore,
L114: 
L115:  | $$c((\psi\circ\varphi)(x_{i}))=\bigcup_{j\in\{i_{1},\dots,i_{k}\}}c(\psi(x_{j}))=\bigcup_{j\in c(\varphi(x_{i}))}c(\psi(x_{j})).$$  |
L116: 
L117: ∎
L529: Hence, a sequence $(X_{1},X_{2},\dots,X_{n})$ is $(\Theta,p)$-pure if and only if for $i>j$, we have $p(X_{i},X_{j})$. These are the so-called monotone sequences as defined in (cite32†Andrenšek, 2025 , Definition 3). In that paper, the endomorphism monoid of $K_{n}$ is shown to be isomorphic to a submonoid of $B_{n}$ of matrices avoiding a certain pattern. They denote this monoid by $D_{n}$. It quickly follows that $\Psi(S_{n}(\Theta,p))$ coincides with $D_{n}$.

L615: In (cite17†Ganyushkin and Mazorchuk, 2011 , Theorem 1(viii)), it is shown that, in this case, $\mathrm{HK}_{\Theta}$ is isomorphic to the Catalan monoid $\mathcal{C}_{n+1}$. The Catalan monoid $\mathcal{C}_{n+1}$ is the monoid of all order-preserving and order-decreasing total transformations of the set $[n+1]$. That is, the set of all $f:[n+1]\to[n+1]$ such that:
L616: 
L617:   1. (i)
L618: 
L619: $f(i)\leq f(j)$ for $i,j\in[n+1]$ with $i\leq j$ (order-preserving);
L620: 
L621:   2. (ii)
L622: 
L623: $f(i)\leq i$ for $i\in[n+1]$ (order-decreasing).
L624: The operation in $\mathcal{C}_{n+1}$ is the usual composition and the unit element is the identity on $[n+1]$. For $f,g\in\mathcal{C}_{n+1}$, we denote by $fg=f\circ g$.
L625: 
L626: Catalan monoids and their presentations were studied in cite57†Solomon (1996) . In (cite58†Stanley, 1999 , 6.25(g)), it was shown that $|\mathcal{C}_{n+1}|=C_{n+1}$, where $C_{n}=\frac{1}{n+1}\binom{2n}{n}$ denotes the $n$-th Catalan number.
